subject: business_studies

provenance.source: NTA master question paper (CBT export with Question IDs and Option IDs), AglaSem Docs copy, downloaded 21 Nov 2026 with the owner's approval
provenance.key: NTA CUET (UG) 2026 final key, matched by Question ID and Option ID; 50 of 50 questions authenticated (5 ids read by eye from the page images)

bankRead: saved READ-ONLY snapshot of 20 Nov 2026 (same as the 2024 check): 394 visible business_studies rows, 209 served (served_bst.json); only served ids cited. No database read in this run.
cards: data/keycards/decks/business_studies.json v7 (902 cards, NCERT Reprint 2026-27; no Financial Markets cards); suspended list empty
syllabus: CUET (UG) 2026 Business Studies (305), data/cuet_syllabus.js: 12 units incl. Financial Markets; no question of this paper falls outside it
rule: strict; Key cards count (answer side only); doubtful = not_covered; match, sequence and multi-statement items need every part; passage-only items = skill
notesForCheckerB: No item was judged skill: every case question (331-340) needs a stored concept the passage does not state.

Calls to re-check: 295 (delegation card omits basis of hierarchy), 298 (HR "most important asset" for "foundation"), 311 (two accepted keys), 313 ("health and sanitation" vs "living"), 318 (application of restricted entry).
Partial (not covered): 317, 319, 320, 338. Elimination would reach the key in 319 and 320, but the strict rule needs every part.

facts: Business environment is largely uncertain (a feature)
Business environment is complex: relatively easier to understand in parts but difficult to grasp in its totality
Business environment includes both specific and general forces, so "only general forces" is false
Business environment is a relative concept

matches.teaches: largely uncertain
complex phenomenon, easier to understand in parts
relative concept
features include specific and general forces
specific and general forces both part of the environment

questions.reason: Cards state all three true features in the paper's own words and list specific and general forces, which rules out (C).

facts: The organising function creates the organisation structure (designing roles and their inter-relationships); staffing then fills those positions

matches.teaches: organisation structure is the outcome of the organising process
organising creates the structural framework within which people work
staffing fills the positions in the structure (rules out staffing)

questions.reason: Card and bank teach that the organisation structure is the outcome of organising; the sentence itself opens the NCERT Staffing chapter, hence the chapter tag.

facts: Staffing order: estimating manpower requirements, recruitment, selection, placement and orientation, training, performance appraisal
(B) analysing jobs to know the need and type of persons = estimating manpower requirements
(C) job advertisement = recruitment
(D) introducing the selected employee and familiarising with rules = orientation
(A) evaluating performance against predetermined standards = performance appraisal

matches.teaches: first five steps in order
performance appraisal follows training
workload analysis assesses number and types of people needed
advertisements are a recruitment source
(D) word for word
(A) word for word

questions.reason: Cards give the order and the meaning of every statement; two statements are card definitions word for word.

facts: Learning the risks of products and using them safely is a consumer responsibility
Filing a complaint in a consumer forum is a consumer responsibility
Respecting the environment is a consumer responsibility
Publishing periodicals is a function of consumer organisations and NGOs, not a consumer responsibility

matches.teaches: items (iii), (viii) and (x): risks, file a complaint, respect the environment
(ii) publishing periodicals and other publications

questions.reason: The responsibilities card has (A), (B) and (C); the NGO-functions card places (D) with consumer organisations.

facts: Flexibility and initiative from divisions working as autonomous units is an advantage of the divisional structure, not of delegation

matches.teaches: flexibility and more initiative are divisional-structure advantages
effective management and growth are delegation benefits (options 1 and 2)

questions.reason: Cards place flexibility and initiative under the divisional structure; note the delegation card omits "basis of management hierarchy" (option 3), so Checker B should look at this call.

facts: Selection tests are intelligence, aptitude, personality, trade and interest tests; there is no "contribution test"

matches.teaches: the five selection tests

questions.reason: Card lists the five tests; contribution test is not one.

facts: Product concept: focus on product quality, performance and features and their continuous improvement

matches.teaches: quality, performance and innovative features = product concept
product improvement is the key under the product concept

questions.reason: Served bank question asks the same idea directly.

facts: Staffing matters because human resources are the most important asset / foundation of a business (right people take it to the top)
Staffing is a continuous process (option 2 false)
Training raises productivity and leads to higher, not lesser, profits (option 4 false)

matches.teaches: human resources are the most important asset of an organisation
staffing is a continuous process
productivity in quantity and quality leading to higher profits

questions.reason: Cards teach the keyed idea (HR the most important asset) and refute options 2 and 4; the "foundation ... break your business" sentence itself is not on a card, so Checker B should look at this call.

facts: Controlling helps in judging accuracy of standards: it checks changes in the organisation and environment and helps review and revise standards

matches.teaches: judging accuracy of standards: verify whether standards are accurate and objective
judging accuracy of standards listed as an importance

questions.reason: Card names and explains this importance of controlling.

facts: Functional differentiation (departments pursuing their own objectives, e.g. production vs sales) is a reason coordination is needed
questions.reason: Coordination is taught widely, but none of growth in size, functional differentiation or specialisation is taught as its importance (not in the NCERT 2026-27 deck).

facts: Overfull demand: demand more than the company can or wants to handle; the marketer reduces it temporarily (less promotion, higher price)

matches.teaches: overfull demand: reduce demand temporarily by cutting promotion or raising prices

questions.reason: Card ties the paper's exact wording to overfull demand; no served bank question asks it.

facts: Policies are standing plans; budgets and projects are single-use plans

matches.teaches: standing plans: policies, procedures, methods, rules
single-use: budgets, programmes, projects

questions.reason: Card lists policies among standing plans and budgets and projects among single-use plans.

facts: Offer for sale: securities are sold to the investing public through intermediaries such as issuing houses or stock brokers
questions.reason: Four served Financial Markets rows, none on methods of floatation; the deck has no Financial Markets cards.

facts: EPS working: EBIT, less interest on debt, = EBT, less tax, = EAT (then divided by number of shares)

matches.teaches: EBIT-EPS names only
interest deductible before tax

questions.reason: Cards name EBIT-EPS analysis and say interest is tax deductible, but no served material lays out the EBIT, interest, EBT, EAT order.

facts: A product gives the customer functional, psychological and social benefits; "marketing benefits" is not one

matches.teaches: functional, psychological, social benefits

questions.reason: Card lists exactly the three benefits.

facts: Treasury bills are issued for a minimum of Rs 25,000 and in multiples thereof
questions.reason: No served bank row or card states the T-bill minimum; the one T-bill mention (cbf7f067) is a wrong option about commercial paper.

facts: Principles are formed by experience and collective wisdom of managers and experimentation
Principles apply to all types of organisations (universal)
Principles are flexible, not rigid prescriptions (C false)
Principles establish cause and effect relationships

matches.teaches: (A) word for word
(B) word for word
not rigid prescriptions
(D) word for word
principles are flexible general guidelines, not rigid rules

questions.reason: Each statement is a card sentence; the bank teaches flexibility too.

facts: Stock exchange functions include liquidity and marketability, safety of transactions, economic growth and providing scope for (healthy) speculation, so a complete stop on speculation is not a function
questions.reason: No served material teaches the functions of a stock exchange.

facts: Planning process order: setting objectives, developing premises, identifying alternatives, ..., follow-up action
Premises = assumptions about the uncertain future

matches.teaches: seven steps in order ending in follow-up action
assumptions about the future are premises
meaning of setting objectives, premises, identifying alternatives

questions.reason: Card gives the order; card and bank give what each step means.

facts: Programmed instruction is an off-the-job method; apprenticeship, coaching and internship are on-the-job

matches.teaches: programmed instruction listed off-the-job
apprenticeship, coaching, internship listed on-the-job

questions.reason: Two cards sort all four options.

facts: NTA accepts two answers. Right to be informed = complete information about the product incl. date of manufacture/expiry
Right to be heard = right to file a complaint and be heard when dissatisfied

matches.teaches: missing expiry date on a pack = right to be informed
information incl. date of manufacture
right to file a complaint and be heard

questions.reason: Both accepted answers are taught; the bank ties an expiry-date problem to the right to be informed. The item itself is ambiguous (two keys), so Checker B should look at this call.

facts: Demat steps: identify a depository participant, complete account opening form and documents, hand physical certificates to the DP with a dematerialisation request, then public-offer allotments are credited to the demat account
questions.reason: The one served demat row (ccf6b28b) is about fraud and the registry, not the steps.

facts: Rising standards (of health and sanitation / living) make packaging important
Self-service outlets make packaging important
Packaging creates product differentiation
Describing the product and specifying its contents is a function of a label, not a reason for packaging

matches.teaches: rising standards, self-service outlets, product differentiation
describe the product and specify its contents is a label function

questions.reason: Cards teach all four; the card says rising standards of "health and sanitation" where the paper says "living", a wording gap Checker B should look at.

facts: Decentralisation must be applied with caution as it can lead to organisational disintegration if departments follow their own guidelines against the organisation's interest

matches.teaches: importance only (reducing burden, initiative ...)

questions.reason: Decentralisation is defined and its importance listed, but the caution about disintegration is taught nowhere.

facts: Harmony, not discord: no class conflict, complete harmony between management and workers (the Japanese black-badge example)

matches.teaches: names Harmony not discord
mental revolution: competition to cooperation

questions.reason: The principle is only named; what it means and the Japanese example are taught nowhere, while two bank rows teach the trap answer, Cooperation not individualism.

facts: Attitudes towards product innovations, lifestyles, occupational distribution and consumer preferences are part of the social environment, not economic

matches.teaches: option 3 word for word under social environment
options 1, 2 and 4 listed as economic

questions.reason: Cards place option 3 under social and the other three under economic.

facts: Reference checks = verifying information and gaining additional information about an applicant
Contract of employment = includes job title, duties, pay, allowances, hours, leave rules etc.
Preliminary screening = eliminating unqualified or unfit applicants from application-form information
Job offer = generally contains a date by which the appointee must report on duty

matches.teaches: (C)-(I) word for word
contract: offer, terms and conditions and date of joining

questions.reason: Partial: screening taught, reference checks only by who acts as referee; the deck's contract card even puts the joining date in the contract, against the key pair (D)-(II).

facts: Requiring specific qualifications to manage reflects management as a profession (restricted entry through an educational degree)

matches.teaches: entry to a profession restricted through an exam or educational degree
features of a profession

questions.reason: Card teaches entry restricted by qualification as a feature of a profession; applying it to managers is the step the item asks.

facts: Method study aims to minimise cost of production and maximise quality and customer satisfaction
Motion study = study of movements like lifting, putting objects, sitting
Fatigue study = amount and frequency of rest intervals
Time study = standard time for a well-defined job

matches.teaches: (B)-(II) word for word
(C)-(IV) word for word
(D)-(I) word for word
method study finds one best way (not the cost/quality aim)

questions.reason: Partial: three pairs taught word for word; method study is taught only as "one best way", never with the cost and customer-satisfaction aim in (III).

facts: Maslow order: physiological, safety, (affiliation), esteem, self-actualisation
Hunger, thirst, shelter, sleep = physiological
Job security, stability of income, pension = safety
Self-respect, autonomy status, recognition, attention = esteem
Drive to become what one is capable of becoming = self-actualisation

matches.teaches: order and esteem description
hunger, thirst, shelter, sleep
job security, stability of income, pension
self-actualisation is the highest need (no meaning)

questions.reason: Partial: three descriptions are on cards word for word, but what self-actualisation means (statement A) is taught nowhere.

facts: Undermines social values, encourages sale of inferior products and confuses buyers are objections to advertising
"Flexible tool" is a merit of personal selling, not a criticism of advertising

matches.teaches: the four objections
undermines social values
inferior products
confuses buyers
flexible tool is a personal-selling point

questions.reason: Cards teach all three objections and place "flexible tool" under personal selling.

facts: Planning leads to rigidity: managers cannot change a pre-decided plan when circumstances change

matches.teaches: planning leads to rigidity as managers stick to a plan when conditions change
leads to rigidity listed first

questions.reason: Served bank question teaches the same limitation with the same reasoning.

matches.teaches: names the objectives only

facts: Management increases efficiency: reducing costs and increasing productivity through better planning, organising, directing, staffing and controlling

matches.teaches: increases efficiency listed as an importance

matches.teaches: same definition word for word
